move: glowing gradient rounded rings rush toward camera from a drifting vanishing point
how: A canvas draws 18 rounded-rectangle rings stacked in depth; each frame their z advances by three ring-spacings per loop (integer, so t=D equals t=0) and they re-enter at the back, scaled by a steep depth^2.6 perspective around a vanishing point that drifts on a small circle. Stroke width, glow (shadowBlur) and alpha grow with depth, and each ring's linear-gradient hue turns 360 degrees per loop. Over the canvas a GSAP timeline spins the logo's rounded-diamond outline 45 to 405 degrees (ease none), pulses the centre dot 0.8 to 1.2 and the glow disc 0.9 to 1.15 with sine.inOut yoyo. Dark radial fog hides the vanishing point.
adapt: Replace the mark and wordmark, set the ring hue offset and the background colour; keep N=18 rings, the 3-rings-per-loop speed and the full logo turn so the loop closes.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, glow and logo inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the logo timeline plus a {u:0->1, duration:D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate paints the rings (replacing the fx.register seek that also called tl.seek). Scope '.mark i', '.mark b', '.glow' to el.
caveats: shadowBlur up to 62px on 18 strokes per frame is expensive
